subject: Qualification: Streaming/Concurrency Targets and Production Readiness plan
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Reynolds <alicia@edgeai.com>
Cc: Tom Park <tom@edgeai.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap: Streaming + concurrency qualification & next steps

Thanks again for carving out time this morning — great conversation. I wanted to capture the highlights, the success criteria you articulated, and immediate next steps so everyone has the same picture. TL;DR: EdgeAI is focused on a streaming-first chat UX, must hit p95 latency targets on first-byte and overall completion, and needs predictable concurrency for a June pilot.

Key pain points (from your team):
- Perceived slow first-byte on streaming chat (users see a ~200–700ms delay before tokens start).
- Back-end bottlenecks when multiple agents spin up (currently seeing tail latency spikes during 100–200 concurrent sessions).
- High unit cost from current inference infra (Hugging Face endpoints + bespoke batching) with limited autoscaling guarantees.

Current stack (what you shared):
- Frontend: React streaming client that renders tokens as they arrive.
- Model infra: self-hosted transformer endpoints on AWS (custom endpoint layer over HF models) + separate orchestrator service. No centralized KV cache; batching currently disabled to preserve streaming UX.
- Observability: basic CloudWatch dashboards, sampling traces by request id (not full token-level traces).

Stated goals / success criteria for pilot (June):
- UX: first-token latency (time-to-first-byte) <= 200ms p95 for short responses (<128 tokens).
- Completion: end-to-end response p95 <= 1200ms for typical 128-token responses; target 95th percentile stable under 200 concurrent streaming sessions.
- Concurrency: sustained 200 concurrent sessions, burstable to 400 for peak events without >2x tail latency increase.
- Cost: reduce per-request compute cost by >=30% vs current baseline.

Immediate asks from EdgeAI to Redwood:
1) We need a short trial config that reproduces your current workload (sample payloads + concurrency profile). Attachment: MVP_requirements.pdf (you mentioned it contains sample prompts and UX traces).
2) Technical deep-dive to validate: (a) where first-byte delay is occurring (client vs network vs model sched), (b) options for preserving streaming UX while enabling batching/caching.
3) Proposal for a trial: Suggested reserved capacity profile and a canary rollout plan with rollback criteria.

Next steps I propose (please confirm):
- Alicia/Tom: share the sample workload file and 24h perf traces (p95/p99 token timing, request ids) by EOD Mon (2027-05-31).
- Redwood: Aditya and Marissa to review traces and propose a trial config (dedicated pool + streaming-optimized model variant) by Tue (2027-06-01).
- Schedule a 60-min technical deep-dive (infra + perf) next week — propose Wed 2027-06-02 09:00 PT.

If that aligns, I'll draft a minimal trial statement of work for legal/procurement and include the acceptance criteria above.

Thanks — Soojin
Soojin Lee
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
soojin@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0198

- MVP_requirements.pdf (6 pages)
From: Alicia Reynolds <alicia@edgeai.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Park <tom@edgeai.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-30T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Streaming + concurrency qualification & next steps

Thanks Soojin — this is great and captures it. A few clarifications and items we can attach: 

Clarifications:
- The 200–700ms first-byte we mentioned is what our EU pilot users are seeing; US users are slightly faster (~150–400ms). We think there's a mix of client-side buffering and server-side queueing.
- Our "200 concurrent sessions" estimate is active simultaneous chat sessions (users often keep a connection open; concurrency measured by active SSE/WS connections).

We will attach: 
- sample_prompts_v2.json (examples of typical user prompts and average response lengths)
- perf_dump_20270529.zip (24h of sampled traces, includes annotations for peak hour)

Regarding timeline: June pilot still sounds right. We can push the deep-dive to Thu (2027-06-03) 10:00 PT if that's easier for your engineering team.

On acceptance criteria — one note: our product manager wants an explicit rollback condition: if p95 completion latency > 2x baseline during the pilot sustained over 10 minutes, we auto-fail the canary. Please include that in the SOW.

Appreciate it — Alicia
Alicia Reynolds
Head of Platform Engineering | EdgeAI
alicia@edgeai.com
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Reynolds <alicia@edgeai.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-30T13:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Streaming + concurrency qualification & next steps

Thanks for the notes and the clarifications, Alicia. A few technical follow-ups from my side so the deep-dive is productive: 

1) Trace format: Can you confirm the tracing ids are consistent across frontend trace -> gateway -> model? If not, we need a mapping table to reconstruct request paths.

2) Token-level timing: The perf_dump sounds like it may be sampled. Ideally we want: time-to-first-byte, first-token duration, per-token intervals for ~100 sample requests across peak and off-peak windows. If sending per-token logs is prohibitive, a small representative subset will work.

3) Current batching strategy: You mentioned batching disabled — please confirm if that is a global flag on the model endpoint or handled in request-router. Knowing whether batching can be toggled per route will shape our proposed options (prefix caching vs micro-batching + streaming flush).

4) Trial parameters: I'm attaching a quick template that we usually use to propose an initial trial pool. The plan we usually recommend for similar customers is: a small dedicated pool (4x A100-equivalent capacity) with streaming-optimized scheduler, token-level KV cache enabled for repeated prefixes, and a conservative autoscale headroom for bursts to 3x baseline.

Attachment stubs:
- redwood-proposed-trial-params.xlsx (1 sheet: capacity, SLOs, rollback conditions)

If you can send the sample traces and the sample prompts, we'll come back with a concrete per-minute RPS/latency projection and a one-page SOW by Tue 2027-06-01.

Aditya
Aditya Rao
Staff Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.com
